text:
maria-g: Hey team — quick sync. We need to lock the burst-smoothing thresholds for the Dedicated pools pilot. Customer asks have been inconsistent: some want aggressive smoothing to avoid throttles, others want tight limits to protect shared reserved capacity. Can we pick the defaults+override rules by EOD? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sanjay_r: I put together a small proposal in the doc but TL;DR: two knobs — smoothing_window_ms (default 5000) and spill_threshold_pct (default 85). Smoothing does exponential decay of instantaneous usage to avoid transient spikes.

alex_zhang: Quick Q: how does this interact with per-tenant burst credits? If smoothing hides spikes, tenants might consume more credits before being preempted.

maria-g: Good point. The plan is smoothing for routing decisions only; billing/crediting still uses raw consumption. That preserves fairness while avoiding flapping on autoscale.

kyle: I ran a sim across 3 customer traces — results look good with smoothing_window_ms=5s and spill_threshold_pct=88. Fewer preemptions, <2% latency regressions. Will share graphs.

ops-bot: [alert] simulated rollout to staging failed at 2026-03-20T15:12:11Z — policy conflict: ReservedPool A had hard cap lower than spill_threshold_pct.

maria-g: Ops note — we need to add validation: spill_threshold_pct must be >= pool_min_reserve_pct. Otherwise the policy allows spill above what pool contract guarantees.

sanjay_r: Agreed. Proposal updated: add validation rule and a per-pool override flag allow_spill_override (requires customer sign-off). Also added launch criteria: (1) canary in prod for 48h with no more than 1% error spike, (2) cost delta < 4% in synthetic load, (3) docs + SDK param exposure.

alex_zhang: For the canary gating, who owns rollback automation? We should wire an automatic revert if latency > SLO for >10m.

kyle: I can add a rollout step in the Console that monitors per-route p50/p95 and triggers revert. Will need a flag in the rollout API.

maria-g: Owners: Product (maria-g) for rollout criteria, Eng-runtime (sanjay_r, kyle) for implementation, Eng-sre for observability gating. Follow-up: set a meeting tomorrow 10am to finalize numbers.

liaison: FYI pinging two customers (Acme + FinCorp) to confirm they accept allow_spill_override workflow.

maria-g: Thanks. Final ask before EOD: thumbs up on defaults smoothing_window_ms=5000, spill_threshold_pct=88, validation rule and allow_spill_override opt-in. If no objections, I'll update the RFC and queue the canary. :thumbsup:

sanjay_r: +1

alex_zhang: +1

kyle: +1

ops-bot: deploybot: canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z (zone: us-west1).
